FOMC’s August 2018 statement is clearly positive: strong labor market, robust consumer spending and business investment, inflation near 2%, and balanced risks. However, the April 2018 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey adds a more nuanced credit backdrop: banks reported wider loan rate spreads (tighter pricing), changes consistent with tighter policies and softer demand in commercial real estate, and largely unchanged standards for qualified jumbo mortgages with mixed-to-softer household loan demand. These SLOOS signals suggest credit conditions were not uniformly easing and could act as a modest headwind to the otherwise strong macro picture. Accordingly, I modestly temper the prior optimism.
